title: DCR Bleeding: Surgical Anatomy, Prevention & Hemostasis
summary: A definitive, textbook-grade clinical guide on managing intraoperative and postoperative epistaxis and orbital hemorrhage during Dacryocystorhinostomy (External and Endonasal DCR). Details vascular anatomy, risk mitigation, packing techniques, and step-by-step hemostatic algorithms.

sections.title: Clinical Overview & Bleeding Dynamics
sections.content: Hemorrhage during or after Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) is the primary cause of intraoperative visualization loss, surgical failure, and early postoperative morbidity. Because the lacrimal sac fossa sits at the vascular interface of the internal and external carotid artery systems, brisk bleeding can arise from dermal, bony, mucosal, or deep nasal structures. Uncontrolled bleeding increases the risk of orbital hematoma, lacrimal flap disruption, scar formation, and operational abort.

branches: External Carotid System: Angular Artery (8-10mm medial to inner canthus), Facial Artery branches, Infraorbital Artery
Internal Maxillary Arterial System: Sphenopalatine Artery (Posterior Lateral Nasal & Septal branches)
Internal Carotid System: Anterior Ethmoidal Artery (24mm posterior to anterior lacrimal crest)
Nasal Mucosal Vascular Plexuses: Kiesselbach Plexus (Anterior Septum), Woodruff Plexus (Posterior Nasal)
Venous Systems: Angular Vein, Ethmoidal Veins, Nasal Mucosal Venous Plexus

Dislodgement of fibrin clot from nasal mucosal flaps

sections.title: Step-by-Step Intraoperative Hemostasis Protocol
content: Step 1: Pre-incision Vasoconstriction — Pack nasal cavity with neuro-patties/gauze soaked in 0.05% Oxymetazoline or 1:10,000 Epinephrine for 10 minutes.
Step 2: Targeted Infiltration — Subperiosteal injection of 2% Lidocaine with 1:100,000 Epinephrine along anterior lacrimal crest and middle turbinate axilla.
Step 3: Direct Cutaneous Hemostasis — Bipolar diathermy at 15-20W for skin edge and sub-Q tissue bleeding; avoid excessive monopolar near the optic canal.
Step 4: Bony Hemostasis — Apply bone wax or suction-cautery to bleeding diploic channels of the maxilla/lacrimal bone during osteotomy.
Step 5: Mucosal Hemostasis — Hem-o-lok clips or suction bipolar cautery for posterior/superior mucosal flaps; insert Surgicel or GelFoam matrix.
Step 6: Packing Prior to Closure — Place expandable PVA sponge (Merocel) or oxidized cellulose against osteotomy site before skin closure.

sections.title: Postoperative Epistaxis Escalation Protocol
content: Step 1: Immediate First Aid — Elevate head of bed to 45°, apply ice pack over nasal bridge, instruct patient to pinch soft nasal cartilages firmly for 15 mins.
Step 2: Systemic Stabilization — Monitor vitals; administer IV Tranexamic Acid (TXA) 1000 mg over 10 min; control BP (target SBP < 130 mmHg) using IV Labetalol.
Step 3: Direct Inspection & Declotting — Clear clots with suction or soft nose blow; perform anterior rhinoscopy/nasal endoscopy with Oxymetazoline spray.
Step 4: Anterior Nasal Packing — Lubricate and insert 8cm Merocel pack or 5.5cm Rapid Rhino hydrocolloid balloon inflated with 10-15 mL saline/air.
Step 5: Posterior Packing & Surgical Exploration — If bleeding persists posteriorly, place Foley catheter balloon (30mL) in nasopharynx; take to OR for SPA cautery or interventional embolization.

sections.title: Critical Surgical Landmarks to Avoid Hemorrhage
content: Angular Artery Course: Runs 8–10 mm medial to the medial canthal tendon. Keep skin incisions straight, vertical, and >8mm from canthus.
The 24-12-6 Rule: Anterior Lacrimal Crest to Anterior Ethmoidal Foramen = 24mm; AE Foramen to Posterior Ethmoidal Foramen = 12mm; PE Foramen to Optic Canal = 6mm.
Axilla of Middle Turbinate: Posterior mucosal boundary for safe osteotomy; superior extension risks Ethmoidal Artery rupture and CSF leak.
Lacrimal Sac Medial Wall: Preserve mucosal flaps intact to wrap osteotomy borders, acting as a natural vascular barrier.

sections.title: Red Flags & Emergency Escalation Signs
content: Rapidly expanding medial canthal or eyelid hematoma (Risk of Compartment Syndrome)
Afferent Pupillary Defect (APD), decreased color vision, or severe retrobulbar pain
Intraocular Pressure (IOP) > 30 mmHg following retrobulbar/orbital bloody tracking
Persistent posterior pharyngeal bleeding unresponsive to bilateral anterior packing
Hemodynamic instability (Tachycardia HR > 110, SBP < 90 mmHg, Syncope)
Clear CSF rhinorrhea intermixed with nasal bleeding (Cribriform plate breach)

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
content: Topical Tranexamic Acid (TXA) Irrigations: Studies demonstrate 40% reduction in intraoperative blood loss during endonasal DCR when using 500mg/5mL TXA-soaked nasal packing.
Potassium Titanyl Phosphate (KTP) & Diode Lasers: Laser-assisted DCR provides automated hemostasis of small mucosal vessels, reducing mean blood loss to <10 mL.
Ultrasonic Bone Scalpel (Piezotome): Allows precise osteotomy creation without mucosal laceration or diploic bone bleeding, significantly preserving tissue planes.
Warm Saline Irrigation Protocols: Intraoperative irrigation with 42°C saline promotes hemostasis by accelerating the coagulation cascade without thermal tissue damage.
